root_cause: Starter v1 deliberately ended at authoring verification. Its manifest binds contracts and Workflows but not executable Skill sources, and the existing activation API can only retrieve a Workflow from the static registry by ID. No provenance-only adapter resolves an installed package into the existing runtime inputs, so the Host cannot execute it without manually copying semantics into global registries.
causal_chain: The Starter manifest contains Skill contracts but no Skill implementation paths.
The package digest ignores non-declaration files, so a SKILL.md could not yet be integrity-bound.
Workflow activation requires require_workflow(workspace, workflow_id) from the static registry.
Harness invocation requires a static composition ID and has no Starter registration selector.
The generic LangGraph runtime and TaskRun bridge exist but have no installed-Starter bootstrap.
A naive implementation would duplicate registry rows or fabricate Skill execution, violating existing authorities.
rejected_hypotheses: Copy Starter Workflows into dev-workflows.json; this creates mutable duplicated registration state and couples projects to the Harness source tree.
Treat a Skill contract as executable instructions; a contract cannot prove real Host execution or produce a valid invocation receipt.
Let natural language choose any Workflow directly; mutating selection must be exact and reviewable.
Build a customer-agent-specific graph runner; the existing LangGraph runtime already owns topology and resume semantics.
affected_boundaries: WorkflowSpec activation by exact compiled source
generic LangGraph and TaskRun execution bootstrap
